findings.description: Since commit 62590065 a metered lane is refused (spend_context_missing) unless dispatch_and_wait receives a SpendContext, and converge() builds one only when its caller passes the new optional `phase`. The only caller that passes `phase` is agent_lane.py (task 5.6). The host inline converge() call in skills/autopilot/SKILL.md (PLAN_REVIEW fallback, about line 567) and the other host review phases pass no phase, and task 6.4 edits only the cloud review-section text. On a host where D5 selects the metered lane (one non-metered lane), every host converge() round therefore refuses the openrouter lane and ends capability_unavailable. The 'A host-path metered review is recorded' scenario can only pass in a unit test that calls dispatch_and_wait directly. Fix: add a task (or extend 6.4) that makes every host converge() caller in skills/autopilot/SKILL.md pass phase=<PLAN_REVIEW|IMPL_REVIEW|VAL_REVIEW>, or have converge() derive a SpendContext from change_id plus review_type and round when phase is None (accepting the IMPL/VAL collision only for that fallback).

Task 5.6 bullet 1 still says converge() 'passes work_unit_ref=<change_id>:<phase>:round-<n> to dispatch_and_wait (via _accepts_kwarg)'. After commit 62590065 the design's interface contract table, D4 and task 3.10 define the keyword as `spend_context: SpendContext(change_id, work_unit_ref)`. Groups 3 and 5 implement the two sides of this keyword in separate packages, so an implementer following 5.6 literally would pass a keyword that ReviewOrchestrator.dispatch_and_wait does not accept, and _accepts_kwarg would silently drop it, which leaves every metered dispatch spend_context_missing.

The D4 per-round budget re-check reads metered_usd_used from GET /routing/usage, which counts only ledger rows. Rows that spooled because POST /routing/spend failed are invisible to it. D4 says 'the key's credit limit bounds spend while rows sit in the spool', but when the key limit is null and the coordinator ceiling is the only source, a worker whose GET succeeds while its POST fails (the partly-forbidden coordinator case D4 itself cites: coordinator_projection_forbidden) keeps passing the re-check while every round's spend spools. The bound then fails exactly in the degraded mode that motivated the spool. The Cost abuse bullet in Security and the Risks row on concurrent overspend do not cover it.
